title: 3.3.4 Lab: Update Scores by Index
description: Reassign values inside an array by their index to update scores in place. Auto-graded: the code runs and the final scores are checked.

steps.title: Start with the scores
steps.instructions: The starter already creates the array: let scores = [72, 85, 90, 64];. Leave that line exactly as it is.

steps.title: Update the first score by index
steps.instructions: One student retook the first test. Reassign the value at index 0 to 77 using scores[0] = ... . Use index assignment, not push or pop, so the array keeps the same length.

steps.title: Raise the last score by index
steps.instructions: The last score (index 3) goes up by 6 points. Update it by its index as well: either scores[3] = 70 or scores[3] += 6 works.

steps.title: Log the whole array
steps.instructions: After both updates, use console.log to print the scores array. Check that the first and last values changed and the middle two did not.

requirements.title: index assignment on scores
requirements.description: Code changes an item of scores by its index (scores[0] = ..., scores[i] += ..., scores[scores.length - 1] = ...), not scores[0] = scores[0]. Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)
requirements.hint: Change an item with its index, like scores[0] = 77. Writing scores[0] = scores[0] changes nothing, and a new array does not count.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)
requirements.hint: After the updates, add console.log(scores); so the array shows in the output.

requirements.title: scores starts as 72, 85, 90, 64
requirements.description: The code creates scores with the four starting values 72, 85, 90, 64 (the line the starter gives you). Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)
requirements.hint: Keep the starter's first line exactly: let scores = [72, 85, 90, 64]; The checks start from those four numbers.

requirements.title: scores ends as 77, 85, 90, 70
requirements.description: After the code runs, scores holds 77, 85, 90, 70: the first value is now 77, the last went up by 6, the middle two are unchanged, and it is still an array of four. Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)
requirements.hint: Run it and compare. Index 0 becomes 77; index 3 goes up by 6 (64 plus 6). Indexes 1 and 2 must stay 85 and 90.

requirements.title: the updated scores are printed
requirements.description: The output shows the updated scores, so 77 and 70 appear in what console.log printed. Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)
requirements.hint: Print the array after BOTH updates, so the new values 77 and 70 are in the output.
